kind: Static HTML/CSS proposals, not simulator captures

screens.title: Year
screens.description: The same twelve-month overview. Sage replaces the red accent. Month positions and tap targets stay the same.

screens.title: Month
screens.description: The existing scrolling month grid at its default density. Calendar colours remain distinct.

screens.title: Month · zoomed out
screens.description: The existing minimum zoom. A label and the overflow count remain in each busy date.

screens.title: Month · zoomed in
screens.description: The existing expanded grid, scrolled to the middle of October. This is a zoom state, not a new mode.

screens.title: Week
screens.description: The same seven columns, all-day area, time axis, and event overlaps. Narrow columns remain narrow.

screens.title: Day
screens.description: The same week strip and single-day timeline. The background, text, and selected date use Warm Sage.

screens.title: Day · overlapping events
screens.description: Events keep their start time, duration, and side-by-side placement. Calendar colours retain their meaning.

screens.title: View menu
screens.description: Keep the existing Year, Month, Day, and Week menu. There is no new tab or filter.

screens.title: Event detail
screens.description: Carry forward the merged event detail design. Keep the date, location, departure, and full details. No arrival margin.

screens.title: Day · no items
screens.description: Retain the date controls and timeline when the day has no items.

screens.title: Calendar · load error
screens.description: Keep the existing error strip and Retry action above the saved timeline. Do not present a failure as an empty day.

screens.title: Month · large text
screens.description: Keep the existing accessible date picker and agenda fallback. Use the same content colours and clear row spacing.

screens.title: Week · large text
screens.description: Keep the existing accessible agenda layout. Dates and items continue vertically through the selected week.

screens.title: Month · dark
screens.description: Warm charcoal, soft cream text, and light sage. Calendar colours retain separate accents.

screens.title: Day · dark
screens.description: The same overlap layout and time axis in the dark palette.

screens.title: Day · small iPhone
screens.description: The same controls on a 375-point iPhone. More of the timeline remains below the visible area.

screens.title: Today · medium
screens.description: The next timed event and tonight’s meal share the top level. The chore count stays secondary.
screens.notes: Tap the event area to open Calendar. Tap the meal area to open Meals. Tap the count or background to open Today.

screens.title: Today · large
screens.description: Dinner, the next two events, and two chore actions. Meals stay above chores.
screens.notes: Chore circles complete tasks. Chore labels open Today. Event rows open Calendar. The dinner panel opens Meals.

screens.title: Tonight · small
screens.description: One answer: what is for dinner? A plain meal symbol works without a recipe photo.
screens.notes: Tap anywhere to open Meals. This proposal does not require a recipe thumbnail or a new image field.

screens.title: Meal plan · medium
screens.description: Today’s three meals. Dinner has emphasis, without hiding breakfast or lunch.
screens.notes: Tap a meal row to open Meals. The current URL opens the Meals destination; it does not select an individual row.

screens.title: Up next · small
screens.description: The next timed event has a large start time, a clear title, and a location.
screens.notes: Tap anywhere to open Calendar. This is a start time, not a departure time.

screens.title: Chores · small
screens.description: A count and an overdue label. Keep detailed completion actions in larger widgets.
screens.notes: Tap anywhere to open Today. The overdue label uses text as well as colour.

screens.title: Chores · medium
screens.description: Two clear chore rows with separate completion circles and names.
screens.notes: Tap a circle to complete the task. Tap the row label to open Today. Retain the existing completion error handling.

screens.title: Today · dark
screens.description: Use the app’s dark tokens on a solid widget surface.

screens.title: Today · tinted
screens.description: A two-tone approximation of a user-selected sage tint. Labels and hierarchy carry the meaning.
screens.notes: WidgetKit owns the final tint. Preserve the accent and primary groups.

screens.title: Today · clear
screens.description: A glass approximation on a wallpaper sample. Keep readable content without extra glass panels inside it.
screens.notes: WidgetKit owns the material, highlights, and vibrancy. This static image is not a native rendering.

screens.title: Today · reduced transparency
screens.description: Keep the same content on a solid surface when translucency is reduced.

screens.title: Today · large text
screens.description: Reduce the content to dinner and a summary. Keep readable type instead of shrinking all the rows.

screens.title: Today · long names
screens.description: Allow a third title line. Omit location text before shrinking the title.

screens.title: Today · empty
screens.description: Use a calm empty state. Open the app for the full week or meal plan.

screens.title: Today · saved data
screens.description: Keep the saved meal and event information. State its age. Do not imply a live countdown.
screens.notes: Disable completion actions in a cached interactive layout until a fresh response arrives.

screens.title: Today · unavailable
screens.description: When no saved data exists, show a connection state instead of zero events.

screens.title: Today · signed out
screens.description: Use one direct instruction to restore the widget.

screens.title: Today · dinner not planned
screens.description: Keep the next event. Use the meal area to show that dinner needs a plan.
screens.notes: Tap the meal area to open Meals. An empty meal slot is not an empty day.

screens.title: Today · small iPhone size
screens.description: The medium family at 321 × 148 points, for a 375 × 667-point iPhone.
screens.notes: Use fewer lines and keep the footer separate. Native text metrics still need a device check.

screens.title: Chores · save pending
screens.description: Keep the chore visible while its completion request is pending.
screens.notes: Proposed transient presentation. The existing intent must confirm the write before the task disappears.

screens.title: Chores · save failed
screens.description: Keep the unchecked task and show a recovery message.
screens.notes: New persistent error presentation requires state shared between the intent and the timeline provider.

screens.title: Lock Screen · inline
screens.description: A meal name and a familiar symbol. No custom background.
screens.notes: Tap opens Meals. The system renders the accessory in a monochrome style.

screens.title: Lock Screen · rectangular
screens.description: The next event and location in two compact lines.
screens.notes: Tap opens Calendar. Do not add a departure estimate without a data contract.

screens.title: Lock Screen · circular
screens.description: A chore count with a text label. There is no progress ring that could imply a completion ratio.

screens.title: Home Screen · context
screens.description: The widget sizes on a 430-point iPhone. The wallpaper and app icons are schematic context.

screens.title: Lock Screen · context
screens.description: Meal, next event, and chore count in the accessory positions. The wallpaper is an original CSS illustration.

screens.title: Lock Screen · private titles
screens.description: A proposed privacy option hides meal and event titles while keeping a useful task count.
screens.notes: New option: hide titles on the Lock Screen. Configure it through a WidgetKit intent. Unlock behaviour follows the system privacy setting.
